status: Prototype numerical/actual-world and native runtime tests passed. First native art VISUALLY REJECTED: still ponds in short grass. Shore/vegetation revision tracked separately in wetland-shores-20261107.json.
scope: Some existing primary pond candidates in wet lowlands become finite irregular shallow wetland complexes with connected hollows and inherited dry high ground. Ordinary ponds elsewhere and finer shallow pools remain separate.

research.application: Distinguish depression wetlands from connected river/groundwater systems; one contained water head per complex.
Woody wetland hummocks and saturated hollows form a mosaic rather than uniform open water.
Keep marsh, wooded swamp and peatland character distinct rather than flooding all wet regions.

geometry.shape: Lobed outline plus world-addressed smooth hummock/hollow pattern. Higher inherited ground retained; one shared constant head. Dry outer collar and bounded footprint.
geometry.admission: Coarse wet setting, actual wet/moist freshwater ground, complete gentle rim survey, no existing water at sampled interior/rim, and reachable interior hollow. Not every wet region becomes open water.

rejected_attempts: First strict 1.5-percent relief gate admitted no complexes at the two selected scenes. Revised design permits gentle inherited slopes but bounds excavation to 1.2m and requires a reachable hollow, rather than cutting the whole slope flat. Broader actual-world sampling is used; some regions legitimately admit none.
limits: Not flood dynamics or a universal water table. Existing lowland/vegetation art still needs visual assessment. New survey/cache cost must be measured in native loading and moving contexts.
